messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Talks have tight schedules, so moderators asked for a timer.

The quiz settings get the time per question: the "Timer minutes" and "Timer seconds" fields (numbers, 0 by default). 0 minutes and 0 seconds means no timer.

With a timer:

- The moderator's big screen shows a countdown in the M:SS format (for example, "1:30" or "0:05") while a question is open. Players don't see the timer.
- The countdown starts when the question opens. Reloading the page doesn't restart it.
- At 0:00, the question finishes by itself, as if the moderator clicked "Finish". The moderator can still click "Finish" earlier.

The timer is a setting of this Quizzy, so it is not part of the export format.


You can execute bash commands and edit files to implement the necessary changes.

## Recommended Workflow

This workflow should be done step-by-step so that you can iterate on your changes and any possible problems.

1. Analyze the codebase by finding and reading relevant files
2. Create a script to reproduce the issue
3. Edit the source code to resolve the issue
4. Verify your fix works by running your script again
5. Test edge cases to ensure your fix is robust
6. Submit your changes and finish your work by issuing the following command: `echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT`.
   Do not combine it with any other command. <important>After this command, you cannot continue working on this task.</important>

1. You issue at least one command
2. The system executes the command(s) in a subshell
3. You see the result(s)
4. You write your next command(s)

- Directory or environment variable changes are not persistent. Every action is executed in a new subshell.

  "output_head": "# Quizzy

A live quiz app for conference talks. The moderator prepares quizzes under
`/moderate` and runs games from the big screen; the audience joins on their phones.

## Run it

```sh
RAILS_ENV=production PORT=3000 \
SECRET_KEY_BASE=... \
QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME=... \
QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD=... \
bin/serve
```

`bin/serve` prepares the databases (under `storage/`) and the assets, then runs the
app in the foreground on all interfaces. `GET /up` returns 200 when the app is ready.

Every page under `/moderate` asks for the moderator's HTTP Basic credentials.

To move a quiz to another Quizzy, use its "Export" page (JSON to copy) and the
"Import quiz" button on `/moderate`. The format is described in `docs/quiz-json-format.md`.

## Run a game

On the quiz page, **Start a game** opens the big screen. Show the join link and the
QR code; the audience opens the link on a phone, types a name and taps **Join**.
Then **Start**, **Finish**, **Next** and **End quiz** move the game along. After
**End quiz** the big screen lists the leaderboard and each phone shows its place and
points. **Top 3** (the number of winners set in the quiz's **Settings**, 3 by default),
**Draw** (for ties) and **Reset winners** pick the prizes; see `docs/prizes.md`. Several
games per quiz are fine (a rehearsal, then the real talk). Open the big screen on
the address the phones can reach, since the join link uses the address in the
browser's address bar.

The rules, the screens and the live updates are described in `docs/live-game.md`.

## Develop and test

```sh
bundle install
bin/rails db:prepare
bin/rails test                       # unit and request tests
bin/rails test:system                # all browser tests (Cuprite + headless Chromium)
bin/rails test test/system/layout_test.rb   # one browser test file
bin/rubocop
bin/brakeman
```

For the browser tests, `BROWSER_PATH` points at Chromium (default `/usr/bin/chromium`).

Design notes, mockups and the reasoning behind decisions live in `docs/`.

# Quizzy: design notes

Living notes for the next steps. The design itself lives in `docs/mockups/`
(style guide, quiz page, question form; `quizzy.css` and the Inter font are the
design's assets). This file records what we built and why.

## Scope of this release

The moderator side only:

- quizzes (list, create, settings, delete)
- questions with text options, ordering, activation, delete
- the preview: a player-style run through the active questions
- export and import of a quiz as JSON, to move it to another conference or to a
  colleague's Quizzy (see `quiz-json-format.md`)

The live game (see `live-game.md`): a game per play of a quiz, the big screen with
the lobby, questions, counts and results, the players' phones (join, answer, see
the result), and live updates everywhere without page reloads.

Built after the first release: the leaderboard after the end, and the prizes (the
number of winners, Top N, Draw, Reset winners). See `prizes.md`.

## Running

`bin/serve` is the only entry point. With `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT`,
`SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`
set, it:

1. checks the variables (exits if one is missing),
2. checks the bundle is satisfied from the local gems (`bundle install --local` as
   fallback, never the network),
3. runs `db:prepare` (creates and migrates every production SQLite database),
4. runs `assets:precompile` into `public/assets`,
5. `exec`s `rails server` on `0.0.0.0:$PORT` in the foreground.

Data lives only under `storage/`: `production.sqlite3` (app), plus the Solid
Cache, Queue and Cable databases. Logs go to STDOUT. `GET /up` is the health check.

## Routes

| Path | Screen |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | redirects to `/moderate` |
| `/moderate` | quiz list, "New quiz" |
| `/moderate/quizzes/new` | quiz form (Title, "Save quiz") |
| `/moderate/quizzes/:id` | quiz page: questions, "Add question", "Settings", "Preview" |
| `/moderate/quizzes/:id/edit` | "Settings": same quiz form, "Delete quiz" (confirm) |
| `/moderate/quizzes/:id/preview` | player-style run of the active questions |
| `/moderate/quizzes/:id/export` | the quiz as JSON in a `<pre>` ("Export" link on the quiz page) |
| `/moderate/import/new` | "Quiz JSON" text area and "Import" ("Import quiz" button on `/moderate`) |
| `POST /moderate/import` | creates a new quiz from the JSON, or re-renders with the errors (422) |
| `POST /moderate/quizzes/:id/games` | "Start a game" on the quiz page (creates a game) |
| `/moderate/games/:id` | the big screen of a game (lobby, questions, results, "The quiz is over") |
| `/moderate/games/:id/live` | the big screen's live fragment (ETag) |
| `POST /moderate/games/:id/start`, `finish`, `next`, `end_quiz` | the game's buttons |
| `/play/:code` | the join link:",
  "output_tail": "t as a `Question`
  and checked with its own validations, so the import and the form cannot drift.
- Errors name the question ("Question 2: Add at least two options"). Type errors
  are reported first; rule checks run only for questions whose fields have the
  right types.
- Export writes exactly title, questions (text, active, options) and options
  (text, correct). No ids, so a copy is a new quiz every time.
- The export `<pre>` is the only `<pre>` on its page. It uses the design's
  `.code-block` class; the import text area uses `.input--code`.

## Labels the QA tests rely on

These strings are exact (visible text, `<label>`, placeholder or aria-label):

- Game buttons: "Start a game" (quiz page), "Start", "Finish", "Next", "End quiz", "Join".
  Fields: "Your name". Texts: "Players: 2", "Question 1 of 3", "Answers: 1 / 2",
  "Your answer", "Hi, Alice!", "The quiz is over", "Waiting for the quiz to start…".
  Details in `live-game.md`.
- Buttons: "New quiz", "Import quiz", "Save quiz", "Add question", "Delete quiz",
  "Add option", "Save question", "Move up", "Move down", "Delete", "Import",
  "Next question", "See score", "Start over". Navigation buttons are real
  `<button>`s (`button_to` with GET), not links.
- Links: "Settings", "Preview", "Export", "Edit".
- Fields: "Title", "Question", "Quiz JSON" (text area), "Option N" (text),
  "Option N is correct" (checkbox), "Active" (checkbox, quiz page and question form).
- Messages: "Add at least two options", "Mark at least one option as correct",
  "Title can't be blank", "Question can't be blank", "Question 1 of 3",
  "Correct!", "Wrong!", "Score: 2/3", "Quiz imported.", "Nothing was imported".
  Import errors are "Question N: " plus the same rule message.

Prize labels (see `prizes.md`): "Number of winners", "Top 3" (N), "Draw", "Reset winners",
"Winner" (leaderboard badge), "You won!", "Place 2 of 5", "3 points".

Insight: the mockups use icon-only buttons (↑ ↓ ✕). Labels stay visible as text
("Move up", "Move down"); the ✕ row remover has an `aria-label` only.

## Front end

- `quizzy.css` is the design file, unchanged. App-specific rules are in
  `app/assets/stylesheets/moderator.css`.
- Propshaft resolves `url()` relative to the CSS file, so the font sits next to
  `quizzy.css`.
- Turbo Drive handles forms. Delete confirmations use `data-turbo-confirm`, which
  Turbo shows with the native `confirm()` dialog.
- `auto-submit` Stimulus controller: the Active switch submits its form on change.
- `option-rows` Stimulus controller: "Add option" appends a row built from a
  `<script type="text/template">` (kept out of the DOM tree so non-JS parsers
  never see its fields); removing a row renumbers the rest.
- Forms carry `required` but `novalidate`, so the browser leaves validation to the
  server messages.
- The option "✕" remover is an extra beyond the brief, from the mockup.

## Production setup insights

- Propshaft does not serve assets in production. `bin/serve` precompiles into
  `public/assets`, and `config.public_file_server` stays on (no proxy in front).
- The default Action Cable config used Redis. It is `solid_cable` on SQLite now,
  so nothing calls an external service. The live pages use it through Turbo Streams
  (see `live-game.md` for the design, the subscription identifiers and the polling).
- QR codes are drawn locally by the `rqrcode` gem as inline SVG (no image library).
- `allow_browser` was removed: player pages run on any phone browser.
- SSL is off (`force_ssl = false`, `assume_ssl = false`), and `config.hosts` is
  cleared so any host name is accepted.
- `config/master.key` and the credentials file are gone; secrets come from the
  environment only. `/config/master.key` is gitignored anyway.
- Gems: `Gemfile.lock` pins the versions preinstalled in the image, so the bundle
  resolves offline. For system tests, Cuprite drives the system Chromium
  (`BROWSER_PATH`, default `/usr/bin/chromium`) instead of Selenium.

## Testing

- `bin/rails test`: model rules, preview state, HTTP Basic access, request flows,
  import/export (`quiz_export_test.rb`, `quiz_import_test.rb`, `integration/import_export_test.rb`),
  the game (`game_test.rb`, `game_moderation_test.rb`, `play_flow_test.rb`), the prizes
  (`leaderboard_test.rb`, `game_prizes_test.rb`, `quiz_test.rb`, `integration/prizes_test.rb`).
- `bin/rails test:system`: browser flows with Cuprite and headless Chromium
  (`test/system`, including `prizes_test.rb`, a whole game with real timing). `bin/rails test test/system/<file>` runs one file. Basic auth
  is answered through Ferrum's `network.authorize`.
- `bin/rubocop` (omakase style), `bin/brakeman`.
- No network needed for any of it, with two exceptions. `bin/brakeman` adds
  `--ensure-latest`, which exits 5 here ("Brakeman 8.1.0 is not the latest
  version 8.1.1") even with no findings; `bundle exec brakeman` gives the real
  result (0 warnings). `bin/bundler-audit` needs the advisory database from
  GitHub, so it cannot run offline.

  and checked with its own validations, so the import and the form cannot drift.
- Errors name the question ("Question 2: Add at least two options"). Type errors
  are reported first; rule checks run only for questions whose fields have the
  right types.
- Export writes exactly title, questions (text, active, options) and options
  (text, correct). No ids, so a copy is a new quiz every time.
- The export `<pre>` is the only `<pre>` on its page. It uses the design's
  `.code-block` class; the import text area uses `.input--code`.

## Labels the QA tests rely on

These strings are exact (visible text, `<label>`, placeholder or aria-label):

- Game buttons: "Start a game" (quiz page), "Start", "Finish", "Next", "End quiz", "Join".
  Fields: "Your name". Texts: "Players: 2", "Question 1 of 3", "Answers: 1 / 2",
  "Your answer", "Hi, Alice!", "The quiz is over", "Waiting for the quiz to start…".
  Details in `live-game.md`.
- Buttons: "New quiz", "Import quiz", "Save quiz", "Add question", "Delete quiz",
  "Add option", "Save question", "Move up", "Move down", "Delete", "Import",
  "Next question", "See score", "Start over". Navigation buttons are real
  `<button>`s (`button_to` with GET), not links.
- Links: "Settings", "Preview", "Export", "Edit".
- Fields: "Title", "Question", "Quiz JSON" (text area), "Option N" (text),
  "Option N is correct" (checkbox), "Active" (checkbox, quiz page and question form).
- Messages: "Add at least two options", "Mark at least one option as correct",
  "Title can't be blank", "Question can't be blank", "Question 1 of 3",
  "Correct!", "Wrong!", "Score: 2/3", "Quiz imported.", "Nothing was imported".
  Import errors are "Question N: " plus the same rule message.

Prize labels (see `prizes.md`): "Number of winners", "Top 3" (N), "Draw", "Reset winners",
"Winner" (leaderboard badge), "You won!", "Place 2 of 5", "3 points".

Insight: the mockups use icon-only buttons (↑ ↓ ✕). Labels stay visible as text
("Move up", "Move down"); the ✕ row remover has an `aria-label` only.

## Front end

- `quizzy.css` is the design file, unchanged. App-specific rules are in
  `app/assets/stylesheets/moderator.css`.
- Propshaft resolves `url()` relative to the CSS file, so the font sits next to
  `quizzy.css`.
- Turbo Drive handles forms. Delete confirmations use `data-turbo-confirm`, which
  Turbo shows with the native `confirm()` dialog.
- `auto-submit` Stimulus controller: the Active switch submits its form on change.
- `option-rows` Stimulus controller: "Add option" appends a row built from a
  `<script type="text/template">` (kept out of the DOM tree so non-JS parsers
  never see its fields); removing a row renumbers the rest.
- Forms carry `required` but `novalidate`, so the browser leaves validation to the
  server messages.
- The option "✕" remover is an extra beyond the brief, from the mockup.

## Production setup insights

- Propshaft does not serve assets in production. `bin/serve` precompiles into
  `public/assets`, and `config.public_file_server` stays on (no proxy in front).
- The default Action Cable config used Redis. It is `solid_cable` on SQLite now,
  so nothing calls an external service. The live pages use it through Turbo Streams
  (see `live-game.md` for the design, the subscription identifiers and the polling).
- QR codes are drawn locally by the `rqrcode` gem as inline SVG (no image library).
- `allow_browser` was removed: player pages run on any phone browser.
- SSL is off (`force_ssl = false`, `assume_ssl = false`), and `config.hosts` is
  cleared so any host name is accepted.
- `config/master.key` and the credentials file are gone; secrets come from the
  environment only. `/config/master.key` is gitignored anyway.
- Gems: `Gemfile.lock` pins the versions preinstalled in the image, so the bundle
  resolves offline. For system tests, Cuprite drives the system Chromium
  (`BROWSER_PATH`, default `/usr/bin/chromium`) instead of Selenium.

## Testing

- `bin/rails test`: model rules, preview state, HTTP Basic access, request flows,
  import/export (`quiz_export_test.rb`, `quiz_import_test.rb`, `integration/import_export_test.rb`),
  the game (`game_test.rb`, `game_moderation_test.rb`, `play_flow_test.rb`), the prizes
  (`leaderboard_test.rb`, `game_prizes_test.rb`, `quiz_test.rb`, `integration/prizes_test.rb`).
- `bin/rails test:system`: browser flows with Cuprite and headless Chromium
  (`test/system`, including `prizes_test.rb`, a whole game with real timing). `bin/rails test test/system/<file>` runs one file. Basic auth
  is answered through Ferrum's `network.authorize`.
- `bin/rubocop` (omakase style), `bin/brakeman`.
- No network needed for any of it, with two exceptions. `bin/brakeman` adds
  `--ensure-latest`, which exits 5 here ("Brakeman 8.1.0 is not the latest
  version 8.1.1") even with no findings; `bundle exec brakeman` gives the real
  result (0 warnings). `bin/bundler-audit` needs the advisory database from
  GitHub, so it cannot run offline.

messages.content:
{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# Prizes: scoring, the leaderboard and the winners

The design notes for what happens after **End quiz**. The live game itself (phases,
buttons, live updates) is in `live-game.md`; the general notes in `design-notes.md`.

## Scoring

- **Each correct answer gives one point.** A question may have several correct
  options; any correct pick gives its one point. Only the **last pick** of a question
  counts, as before.
- **Speed.** The time of an answer runs from the moment its question opened
  (`game_questions.opened_at`, set on the server when the moderator clicks Start or
  Next) to the player's last pick (`answers.picked_at`). Each pick stamps `picked_at`,
  even when the option stays the same, because `updated_at` does not move then.
  A player's speed is the **total** of the times of their **correct** answers, in whole
  microseconds (`players.speed_micros`). Only the server's clock is used.
- **Ranking** (`Leaderboard.rank`): more points first. Equal points: the lower total
  speed wins. Still equal: the player who joined first wins, so places are always
  distinct and numbered 1..n.
- **Players see no points or places during the game.** Points and places appear only
  after the end. Phones show "Correct!" or "Wrong!" per question, as before. That says
  nothing about the points.

## When the results are stored

`Game#end_quiz!` ranks the players inside the same transaction as the move to `ended`,
and stores `points`, `speed_micros` and `place` on each player. After that, answers are
refused (`answer!` checks the phase inside its transaction), so the stored result cannot
go stale. It is stored rather than recomputed because every phone fetches its place on
each tick, and the ranking would otherwise be redone for every phone.

## Winners

Chosen by the moderator on the big screen, **after the end only**. Before the end,
"Top N", "Draw" and "Reset winners" are refused with "The winners are picked after
the quiz is over."

- **Top N** (the button reads "Top 3" for 3 winners): the first N places that have
  points.
- **Draw** (ties): everyone with more points than the N-th place wins. The remaining
  prizes are drawn at random among the players with exactly the N-th place's points.
  Speed does not count there. Each click draws again and replaces the previous winners.
- **Players with 0 points never win**, with either button. If fewer than N players have
  points, all of them win. If nobody has points, nobody wins and the moderator is told
  "No player has points, so nobody wins."
- **Reset winners** clears every winner.

N is `quizzes.winners_count`, read from the quiz at each click (`Game#winners_count`),
not copied when the game starts. So a change in the quiz settings applies until the
winners are picked. This is a deliberate choice: the moderator who changes the number
expects it to count at the moment they pick.

Each winner action runs in one transaction, so the screens and phones get the same
result. It bumps `revision` (big screen) and `progress` (phones), and ticks both
streams. Measured against `bin/serve` (solid_cable), a phone shows a new winner about
130 ms after the click.

## The settings field

- **Number of winners**: a whole number from 1 to 1000 (`Quiz::MAX_WINNERS_COUNT`).

# Prizes: scoring, the leaderboard and the winners

The design notes for what happens after **End quiz**. The live game itself (phases,
buttons, live updates) is in `live-game.md`; the general notes in `design-notes.md`.

## Scoring

- **Each correct answer gives one point.** A question may have several correct
  options; any correct pick gives its one point. Only the **last pick** of a question
  counts, as before.
- **Speed.** The time of an answer runs from the moment its question opened
  (`game_questions.opened_at`, set on the server when the moderator clicks Start or
  Next) to the player's last pick (`answers.picked_at`). Each pick stamps `picked_at`,
  even when the option stays the same, because `updated_at` does not move then.
  A player's speed is the **total** of the times of their **correct** answers, in whole
  microseconds (`players.speed_micros`). Only the server's clock is used.
- **Ranking** (`Leaderboard.rank`): more points first. Equal points: the lower total
  speed wins. Still equal: the player who joined first wins, so places are always
  distinct and numbered 1..n.
- **Players see no points or places during the game.** Points and places appear only
  after the end. Phones show "Correct!" or "Wrong!" per question, as before. That says
  nothing about the points.

## When the results are stored

`Game#end_quiz!` ranks the players inside the same transaction as the move to `ended`,
and stores `points`, `speed_micros` and `place` on each player. After that, answers are
refused (`answer!` checks the phase inside its transaction), so the stored result cannot
go stale. It is stored rather than recomputed because every phone fetches its place on
each tick, and the ranking would otherwise be redone for every phone.

## Winners

Chosen by the moderator on the big screen, **after the end only**. Before the end,
"Top N", "Draw" and "Reset winners" are refused with "The winners are picked after
the quiz is over."

- **Top N** (the button reads "Top 3" for 3 winners): the first N places that have
  points.
- **Draw** (ties): everyone with more points than the N-th place wins. The remaining
  prizes are drawn at random among the players with exactly the N-th place's points.
  Speed does not count there. Each click draws again and replaces the previous winners.
- **Players with 0 points never win**, with either button. If fewer than N players have
  points, all of them win. If nobody has points, nobody wins and the moderator is told
  "No player has points, so nobody wins."
- **Reset winners** clears every winner.

not copied when the game starts. So a change in the quiz settings applies until the
winners are picked. This is a deliberate choice: the moderator who changes the number

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# Quiz JSON: export and import

Moderators move a quiz to another conference, or share it with a colleague who
runs Quizzy too, as JSON:

- **Export**: the quiz page's "Export" link opens `/moderate/quizzes/:id/export`,
  which shows the quiz as JSON inside the page's only `<pre>`, ready to copy.
- **Import quiz**: the "Import quiz" button on `/moderate` opens
  `/moderate/import/new` with a "Quiz JSON" text area and the "Import" button.
  `POST /moderate/import` creates a **new** quiz (even if one with the same title
  exists) and opens its page with "Quiz imported.".

## Format

```json
{
  "title": "Frontend Fest 2026",
  "questions": [
    {
      "text": "Which HTTP status code means \"Too Many Requests\"?",
      "active": true,
      "options": [
        {"text": "418", "correct": false},
        {"text": "429", "correct": true}
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The number of winners is a setting of the quiz ("Number of winners", see
`prizes.md`). It is not in the export, so an imported quiz gets the default, 3.

Export writes exactly these keys, in this order, and nothing else (no ids, no
timestamps, no positions): the quiz `title`, then its `questions` (all of them,
inactive ones included), each with `text`, `active` and `options`, and each option
with `text` and `correct`. Questions and options keep their order. An empty quiz
exports `"questions": []`.

## Import rules

The document is checked completely before anything is written. The quiz and its
questions are saved in one transaction, so a document that breaks a rule creates
nothing: not the quiz, not part of its questions. The error page lists every
problem it found, each question's problems prefixed with the question number.

- `title`: required, trimmed, at most 200 characters (the quiz form's rule).
  Messages: "Title can't be blank", "Title must be a string".
- `questions`: required list (`[]` is fine). Message: "Questions must be a list".
- `text` of a question: required, trimmed (the question form's rule). Message:
  "Question N: Question can't be blank".
- `active`: optional, `true` by default. Must be `true` or `false`.
- `options`: required list. Message: "Question N: Options must be a list".

# Quiz JSON: export and import

Moderators move a quiz to another conference, or share it with a colleague who
runs Quizzy too, as JSON:

- **Export**: the quiz page's "Export" link opens `/moderate/quizzes/:id/export`,
  which shows the quiz as JSON inside the page's only `<pre>`, ready to copy.
- **Import quiz**: the "Import quiz" button on `/moderate` opens
  `/moderate/import/new` with a "Quiz JSON" text area and the "Import" button.
  `POST /moderate/import` creates a **new** quiz (even if one with the same title
  exists) and opens its page with "Quiz imported.".

## Format

```json
{
  "title": "Frontend Fest 2026",
  "questions": [
    {
      "text": "Which HTTP status code means \"Too Many Requests\"?",
      "active": true,
      "options": [
        {"text": "418", "correct": false},
        {"text": "429", "correct": true}
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The number of winners is a setting of the quiz ("Number of winners", see
`prizes.md`). It is not in the export, so an imported quiz gets the default, 3.

Export writes exactly these keys, in this order, and nothing else (no ids, no
timestamps, no positions): the quiz `title`, then its `questions` (all of them,
inactive ones included), each with `text`, `active` and `options`, and each option
with `text` and `correct`. Questions and options keep their order. An empty quiz
exports `"questions": []`.

## Import rules

The document is checked completely before anything is written. The quiz and its
questions are saved in one transaction, so a document that breaks a rule creates
nothing: not the quiz, not part of its questions. The error page lists every
problem it found, each question's problems prefixed with the question number.

- `title`: required, trimmed, at most 200 characters (the quiz form's rule).
  Messages: "Title can't be blank", "Title must be a string".
- `questions`: required list (`[]` is fine). Message: "Questions must be a list".
- `text` of a question: required, trimmed (the question form's rule). Message:

- Keys other than these are ignored, so an export from a newer version still
  imports.
- Invalid JSON, or a top level that is not an object: "Quiz JSON is not valid
  JSON" / "Quiz JSON must be an object with "title" and "questions"".
- Rules about types are reported first. Rule checks (blank text, option counts) run
  only for questions whose fields have the right types, so the messages do not
  pile up on one mistake.

## Where the code lives

- `app/models/quiz_export.rb`: `QuizExport`, the export shape (`to_h`,
  `pretty_json`).
- `app/models/quiz_import.rb`: `QuizImport`, parsing and checks; `save` creates

# One play of a quiz: its own players, answers and questions.
#
# A game copies the quiz's active questions and their options when it is
# created (see .create_from_quiz!), so editing the quiz later changes neither a
# running game nor one that was already played. Inactive questions are skipped.
#
# Phases, in order (the moderator's button is in brackets):
#
#   lobby   players join; nothing is open yet                      [Start]
#   open    question #position accepts answers                    [Finish]
#   closed  question #position is closed; the answers are shown   [Next], or [End quiz] on the last one
#   ended   the quiz is over: nobody joins or answers any more    (the leaderboard, then the winners)
#
# Players may join in any phase but "ended".
#
# Ending ranks the players and stores each one's result (points, speed, place) on
# the player (see Leaderboard). After the end the moderator picks the winners
# (Top N, Draw, Reset winners). The winners can change any number of times.
#
# Live updates (see application.js): every change bumps `revision` and ticks the
# big screen, which shows the counts. A move (start, finish, next, end) and a
# change of winners bump `progress` and tick the phones too, so a room of phones
# does not refetch on every answer.
class Game < ApplicationRecord
  PHASES = %w[lobby open closed ended].freeze
  # No 0, O, 1 or I: the code is read aloud and typed on phones.
  CODE_ALPHABET = %w[A B C D E F G H J K M N P Q R S T U V W X Y Z 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9].freeze
  CODE_LENGTH = 5
  # What the server sends to a live page: "something changed, fetch your view".
  TICK = '<turbo-stream action="tick"></turbo-stream>'.freeze

  belongs_to :quiz, inverse_of: :games
  has_many :game_questions, -> { order(:position) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :game
  has_many :players, -> { order(:id) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :game

  normalizes :title, with: ->(title) { title.strip }

  validates :title, presence: true
  validates :code, presence: true, uniqueness: true, format: { with: /\A[A-Z2-9]{#{CODE_LENGTH}}\z/ }
  validates :phase, inclusion: { in: PHASES }
  validates :position, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0 }

  before_validation :assign_code, on: :create

  # Creates a game from the quiz's active questions, with their options.
  def self.create_from_quiz!(quiz)
    transaction do
      game = create!(quiz: quiz, title: quiz.title)
      quiz.questions.active.includes(:options).each.with_index(1) do |question, position|
        game_question = game.game_questions.create!(position: position, text: question.text)
        question.options.each.with_index(1) do |option, option_position|
          game_question.options.create!(position: option_position, text: option.text, correct: option.correct)
        end
      end
      game
    end
  end

  # A code that no game uses yet.
  def self.unused_code
    loop do
      code = Array.new(CODE_LENGTH) { CODE_ALPHABET[SecureRandom.random_number(CODE_ALPHABET.size)] }.join
      return code unless exists?(code: code)
    end
  end

  # Names of the Action Cable streams the live pages subscribe to.
  def live_stream_name = "quizzy_game_#{id}"
  def play_stream_name = "quizzy_game_#{id}_play"

  def lobby? = phase == "lobby"
  def open? = phase == "open"
  def closed? = phase == "closed"
  def ended? = phase == "ended"

  def total_questions
    game_questions.count
  end

  def last_question?
    position == total_questions
  end

  # The question on screen (open or closed), or nil in t",
  "output_tail": "ount
  end

  # How many players have answered the question on screen.
  def answers_count
    current_question ? current_question.answers.count : 0
  end

  # The player's pick for the question on screen, if any.
  def answer_of(player)
    question = current_question
    question && player && player.answer_for(question)
  end

  # The players in place order. Only meaningful after the end, when the places
  # are stored.
  def ranked_players
    players.reorder(:place, :id).to_a
  end

  # How many winners the moderator asked for. It is read from the quiz as it is
  # now, so a change in the settings applies until the winners are picked.
  def winners_count
    Quiz.where(id: quiz_id).pick(:winners_count)
  end

  # Moderator actions. Each returns true when the game moved, and false when it
  # was not in a phase that allows the action (for example, a second click on
  # "Finish"). The state is read again inside the transaction, so two moderators
  # clicking at once cannot move the game twice.

  def start!
    move { [ "open", 1 ] if lobby? && total_questions.positive? }
  end

  def finish!
    move { [ "closed", position ] if open? }
  end

  def next_question!
    move { [ "open", position + 1 ] if closed? && position < total_questions }
  end

  def end_quiz!
    move { [ "ended", position ] if lobby? || closed? }
  end

  # Winner actions, after the end only. Each returns the new winners (an array,
  # possibly empty), or nil when the game is not over. The winners are chosen and
  # stored in one transaction, so the screens and phones get the same answer.

  def pick_top_winners!
    choose_winners { |ranked| Leaderboard.top(ranked, winners_count) }
  end

  def draw_winners!
    choose_winners { |ranked| Leaderboard.draw(ranked, winners_count) }
  end

  def reset_winners!
    choose_winners { [] }
  end

  # Player actions.

  # Adds a player. Returns the player. It is unsaved, with errors, when the name
  # is not valid or the quiz is over.
  def join(name)
    player = players.new(name: name)
    saved = transaction do
      next false if Game.where(id: id, phase: "ended").exists?

      player.save && bump_revision!
    end
    broadcast_change if saved
    player
  end

  # Records the player's pick for the question on screen. The last pick counts,
  # and its time is kept (picked_at) for the speed ranking. Returns false when the
  # question is not open, or the option is not on it.
  def answer!(player, option)
    saved = transaction do
      reload
      question = current_question
      next false unless open? && question && option.game_question_id == question.id && player.game_id == id

      Answer.find_or_initialize_by(player: player, game_question: question)
            .update!(game_option: option, picked_at: Time.current)
      bump_revision!
    end
    broadcast_change if saved
    saved
  end

  private

  def assign_code
    self.code = self.class.unused_code if code.blank?
  end

  # Runs the block with the freshly read game. The block returns [phase, position]
  # for the move, or nil when the move is not allowed from the current state.
  def move
    moved = transaction do
      reload
      target_phase, target_position = yield
      next false unless target_phase

      now = Time.current

#
#   lobby   players join; nothing is open yet                      [Start]
#   open    question #position accepts answers                    [Finish]
#   closed  question #position is closed; the answers are shown   [Next], or [End quiz] on the last one
#   ended   the quiz is over: nobody joins or answers any more    (the leaderboard, then the winners)
#
# Players may join in any phase but "ended".
#
# Ending ranks the players and stores each one's result (points, speed, place) on
# the player (see Leaderboard). After the end the moderator picks the winners
# (Top N, Draw, Reset winners). The winners can change any number of times.
#
# Live updates (see application.js): every change bumps `revision` and ticks the

# change of winners bump `progress` and tick the phones too, so a room of phones

  CODE_LENGTH = 5

  scope :active, -> { where(active: true) }

  validates :text, presence: true
  validate :validate_option_rows, if: -> { @option_rows }

  before_create :place_at_end
  after_save :save_option_rows, if: -> { @option_rows }

  # Rows as typed in the form: [{ text:, correct: }, ...], in display order.
  # Assigning rows does not touch the database until the question is saved.
  attr_reader :option_rows

  def option_rows=(rows)
    @option_rows = Array(rows).map do |row|
      { text: row[:text].to_s, correct: ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(row[:correct]) == true }
    end
  end

  # Rows to show in the form: what was typed, or the saved options, padded to
  # FORM_OPTION_ROWS so the form always has room for new options.
  def form_option_rows
    rows = @option_rows || options.map { |option| { text: option.text, correct: option.correct } }
    rows + Array.new([ FORM_OPTION_ROWS - rows.size, 0 ].max) { { text: "", correct: false } }
  end

  def move_up
    move_by(-1)
  end

  def move_down
    move_by(1)
  end

  private

  def kept_option_rows
    (@option_rows || []).select { |row| row[:text].strip.present? }
  end

  def validate_option_rows
    kept = kept_option_rows
    errors.add(:base, "Add at least two options") if kept.size < MIN_OPTIONS
    errors.add(:base, "Mark at least one option as correct") if kept.none? { |row| row[:correct] }
  end

    Option.where(question_id: id).delete_all
    kept_option_rows.each.with_index(1) do |row, position|
      Option.create!(question: self, text: row[:text].strip, correct: row[:correct], position: position)
    end

    index = ordered.index { |question| question.id == id }
    target = index && index + step
    return if index.nil? || target.negative? || target >= ordered.size

    ordered[index], ordered[target] = ordered[target], ordered[index]
    Question.transaction do
      ordered.each.with_index(1) do |question, position|
        question.update_column(:position, position) unless question.position == position
      end
    end
    reload
  end

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "module Moderate
  # The moderator's side of a live game: starting one from a quiz, the big-screen
  # page, the buttons that move the game on (Start, Finish, Next, End quiz), and
  # the prizes after the end (Top N, Draw, Reset winners).
  class GamesController < BaseController
    before_action :set_game, except: :create

    MOVED_ON = "The game has already moved on. Look at the screen.".freeze
    NOT_OVER = "The winners are picked after the quiz is over.".freeze
    NOBODY_WINS = "No player has points, so nobody wins.".freeze

    # "Start a game" on the quiz page.
    def create
      game = Game.create_from_quiz!(Quiz.find(params[:quiz_id]))
      redirect_to moderate_game_path(game), status: :see_other
    end

    # The big screen.
    def show
      render layout: "screen"
    end

    # The part of the big screen that changes. The page fetches it on every tick.
    # The winners count is part of the ETag: it can change in the quiz settings.
    def live
      render partial: "moderate/games/screen", locals: { game: @game } if stale?(etag: [ @game.revision, @game.winners_count ])
    end

    def start
      if @game.start!
        back_to_screen
      elsif @game.lobby?
        back_to_screen(alert: "This quiz has no active questions to play.")
      else
        back_to_screen(alert: MOVED_ON)
      end
    end

    def finish
      back_to_screen(alert: @game.finish! ? nil : MOVED_ON)
    end

    def next_question
      back_to_screen(alert: @game.next_question! ? nil : MOVED_ON)
    end

    def end_quiz
      back_to_screen(alert: @game.end_quiz! ? nil : MOVED_ON)
    end

    def top_winners
      winners_picked(@game.pick_top_winners!)
    end

    def draw_winners
      winners_picked(@game.draw_winners!)
    end

    def reset_winners
      back_to_screen(alert: @game.reset_winners!.nil? ? NOT_OVER : nil)
    end

    private

    def set_game
      @game = Game.find(params[:id])
    end

    def winners_picked(winners)
      back_to_screen(alert: winners_alert(winners))
    end

    # Nil: the game is not over. Empty: the draw had nobody with points to pick.
    def winners_alert(winners)
      return NOT_OVER if winners.nil?
      return NOBODY_WINS if winners.empty?

      nil
    end

    def back_to_screen(alert: nil)

module Moderate
  # The moderator's side of a live game: starting one from a quiz, the big-screen
  # page, the buttons that move the game on (Start, Finish, Next, End quiz), and
  # the prizes after the end (Top N, Draw, Reset winners).
  class GamesController < BaseController
    before_action :set_game, except: :create

    MOVED_ON = "The game has already moved on. Look at the screen.".freeze
    NOT_OVER = "The winners are picked after the quiz is over.".freeze
    NOBODY_WINS = "No player has points, so nobody wins.".freeze

    # "Start a game" on the quiz page.
    def create
      game = Game.create_from_quiz!(Quiz.find(params[:quiz_id]))
      redirect_to moderate_game_path(game), status: :see_other
    end

    # The big screen.
    def show
      render layout: "screen"
    end

    # The part of the big screen that changes. The page fetches it on every tick.
    # The winners count is part of the ETag: it can change in the quiz settings.
    def live
      render partial: "moderate/games/screen", locals: { game: @game } if stale?(etag: [ @game.revision, @game.winners_count ])
    end

    def start
      if @game.start!
        back_to_screen
      elsif @game.lobby?
        back_to_screen(alert: "This quiz has no active questions to play.")
      else
        back_to_screen(alert: MOVED_ON)
      end
    end

    def finish
      back_to_screen(alert: @game.finish! ? nil : MOVED_ON)
    end

    def next_question
      back_to_screen(alert: @game.next_question! ? nil : MOVED_ON)
    end

    def end_quiz
      back_to_screen(alert: @game.end_quiz! ? nil : MOVED_ON)
    end

    def top_winners
      winners_picked(@game.pick_top_winners!)
    end

    def draw_winners
      winners_picked(@game.draw_winners!)
    end

    def reset_winners
      back_to_screen(alert: @game.reset_winners!.nil? ? NOT_OVER : nil)
    end

    private

    def set_game
      @game = Game.find(params[:id])
    end

    def winners_picked(winners)
      back_to_screen(alert: winners_alert(winners))
    end

    # Nil: the game is not over. Empty: the draw had nobody with points to pick.
    def winners_alert(winners)
      return NOT_OVER if winners.nil?
      return NOBODY_WINS if winners.empty?

      nil
    end

    def back_to_screen(alert: nil)
      redirect_to moderate_game_path(@game), alert: alert, status: :see_other
    end
  end
end

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Quizzy: prepare the app and run it in production mode, in the foreground.
#
#   RAILS_ENV=production PORT=3000 SECRET_KEY_BASE=... \
#   QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME=... QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD=... bin/serve
#
# Everything the app needs lives under storage/ (SQLite databases) and
# public/assets (precompiled files). Nothing here talks to external services.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export RAILS_ENV="${RAILS_ENV:-production}"
export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"

for name in SECRET_KEY_BASE QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD; do
  if [ -z "${!name:-}" ]; then
    echo "bin/serve: $name must be set" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

# Gems come from the local installation; resolving them must not need the network.
bundle check >/dev/null 2>&1 || bundle install --local

mkdir -p storage tmp/pids log
rm -f tmp/pids/server.pid

bin/rails db:prepare
bin/rails assets:precompile

exec bin/rails server --environment "$RAILS_ENV" --binding 0.0.0.0 --port "$PORT" --pid tmp/pids/server.pid
----
The Gemfile's dependencies are satisfied

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Quizzy: prepare the app and run it in production mode, in the foreground.
#
#   RAILS_ENV=production PORT=3000 SECRET_KEY_BASE=... \
#   QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME=... QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD=... bin/serve
#
# Everything the app needs lives under storage/ (SQLite databases) and
# public/assets (precompiled files). Nothing here talks to external services.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export RAILS_ENV="${RAILS_ENV:-production}"
export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"

for name in SECRET_KEY_BASE QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD; do
  if [ -z "${!name:-}" ]; then
    echo "bin/serve: $name must be set" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

# Gems come from the local installation; resolving them must not need the network.
bundle check >/dev/null 2>&1 || bundle install --local

mkdir -p storage tmp/pids log
rm -f tmp/pids/server.pid

bin/rails db:prepare
bin/rails assets:precompile

exec bin/rails server --environment "$RAILS_ENV" --binding 0.0.0.0 --port "$PORT" --pid tmp/pids/server.pid

module GamesHelper
  # The join link as the moderator shows it: the full URL without the scheme,
  # for example "localhost:3000/play/K7RZX".
  def join_link_text(game)
    play_url(game.code).delete_prefix("http://").delete_prefix("https://")
  end

  # The QR code of the full join link (with the scheme, so a phone camera opens it),
  # as inline SVG that scales with its box.
  def join_qr_code(game)
    svg = RQRCode::QRCode.new(play_url(game.code)).as_svg(module_size: 8, standalone: true, use_path: true, viewbox: true)
    svg.sub(/\A<\?xml[^>]*\?>/, "").html_safe
  end

  # The big-screen background for each phase.
  def screen_cover_class(game)
    case game.phase
    when "lobby" then "cover--blue"
    when "open" then ""
    else "cover--night"
    end
  end

  # Moderator list: the status of a game in words, and the badge class for it.
  def game_status_label(game)
    { "lobby" => "Waiting", "open" => "Running", "closed" => "Running", "ended" => "Finished" }.fetch(game.phase)
  end

  def game_badge_class(game)
    { "lobby" => "", "open" => "badge--running", "closed" => "badge--running", "ended" => "badge--finished" }.fetch(game.phase)
  end

  # What the player sees after a question is closed: [label, status tone].
  def answer_result(answer)
    if answer.nil?
      [ "No answer", "neutral" ]
    elsif answer.game_option.correct?
      [ "Correct!", "right" ]
    else
      [ "Wrong!", "wrong" ]
    end
  end

  # The stream a live page listens to. Each page load gets its own subscription: Action
  # Cable keeps one subscription per identifier, and Turbo's identifier is only the
  # stream name, so the unsubscribe of the page being left could remove the subscription
  # of the page that replaces it. The random attribute makes each identifier unique.
  def live_subscription(stream)
    turbo_stream_from stream, data: { subscription: SecureRandom.hex(8) }
  end

  # Share of the answers an option got, in percent (for the bar on the big screen).
  def answer_share(count, total)
    total.zero? ? 0 : (count * 100.0 / total).round
  end

module GameFixtures

      [ "Left out for now", [ [ "Yes", true ], [ "No", false ] ], false ],
      [ "Which protocol keeps a two-way connection?", [ [ "WebSocket", true ], [ "SMTP", false ] ], true ],
      [ "What does CSS stand for?", [ [ "Cascading Style Sheets", true ], [ "Computer Style System", false ] ], true ]
    ]
    questions.each do |text, options, active|
      question = quiz.questions.new(text: text, active: active)
      question.option_rows = options.map { |label, correct| { text: label, correct: correct } }
      question.save!
    end
    quiz
  end

require "test_helper"

class GameTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  include ActionCable::TestHelper
  include GameFixtures

  setup do
    @quiz = build_quiz_with_questions # three active questions, one inactive
    @game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)
  end

  test "a game copies the active questions and their options, in order" do
    assert_equal [ "Which HTTP status code means \"Too Many Requests\"?",
                   "Which protocol keeps a two-way connection?",
                   "What does CSS stand for?" ], @game.game_questions.map(&:text)
    assert_equal [ 1, 2, 3 ], @game.game_questions.map(&:position)
    assert_equal %w[418 429 503], @game.game_questions.first.options.map(&:text)
    assert_equal [ false, true, false ], @game.game_questions.first.options.map(&:correct)
    assert_equal 3, @game.total_questions
    assert_equal "Frontend Fest 2026", @game.title
  end

  test "editing the quiz later does not change a game" do
    question = @quiz.questions.find_by!(text: "What does CSS stand for?")
    question.update!(text: "Changed")
    question.option_rows = [ { text: "Other", correct: true }, { text: "Nope", correct: false } ]
    question.save!

    @game.reload
    assert_equal "What does CSS stand for?", @game.game_questions.last.text
    assert_equal "Cascading Style Sheets", @game.game_questions.last.options.first.text
  end

  test "a game gets a short code that is unique" do
    assert_match(/\A[A-Z2-9]{5}\z/, @game.code)
    other = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)
    assert_not_equal @game.code, other.code
  end

  test "a new game is in the lobby" do
    assert @game.lobby?
    assert_equal 0, @game.position
    assert_nil @game.current_question
  end

  test "start opens the first question" do
    assert @game.start!
    @game.reload
    assert @game.open?
    assert_equal 1, @game.position
    assert_equal "Which HTTP status code means \"Too Many Requests\"?", @game.current_question.text
    assert_not_nil @game.game_questions.first.opened_at
  end

  test "a game with no active questions cannot start" do
    empty = Game.create_from_quiz!(Quiz.create!(title: "Empty"))
    assert_not empty.start!
    assert empty.lobby?
  end

  test "finish closes the question, and only an open question can be finished" do
    @game.start!
    assert @game.finish!
    @game.reload
    assert @game.closed?
    assert_not_nil @game.game_questions.first.closed_at
    assert_not @game.finish!, "a second Finish does nothing"
  end

  test "next opens the following question, and only after a closed one" do
    assert_not @game.next_question!, "the lobby has no next question"
    @game.start!
    assert_not @game.next_question!, "an open question is not closed yet"
    @game.finish!
    assert @game.next_question!
    @game.reload
    assert_equal 2, @game.position
    assert @game.open?
    assert_equal "Which protocol keeps a two-way connection?", @game.current_question.text
  end

      [ "What does CSS stand for?", [ [ "Cascading Style Sheets", true ], [ "Computer Style System", false ] ], true ]
    ]
    questions.each do |text, options, active|

require "test_helper"

class GameTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  include ActionCable::TestHelper
  include GameFixtures

  setup do
    @quiz = build_quiz_with_questions # three active questions, one inactive
    @game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)
  end

  test "a game copies the active questions and their options, in order" do
    assert_equal [ "Which HTTP status code means \"Too Many Requests\"?",
                   "Which protocol keeps a two-way connection?",
                   "What does CSS stand for?" ], @game.game_questions.map(&:text)
    assert_equal [ 1, 2, 3 ], @game.game_questions.map(&:position)
    assert_equal %w[418 429 503], @game.game_questions.first.options.map(&:text)
    assert_equal [ false, true, false ], @game.game_questions.first.options.map(&:correct)
    assert_equal 3, @game.total_questions
    assert_equal "Frontend Fest 2026", @game.title
  end

  test "editing the quiz later does not change a game" do
    question = @quiz.questions.find_by!(text: "What does CSS stand for?")
    question.update!(text: "Changed")
    question.option_rows = [ { text: "Other", correct: true }, { text: "Nope", correct: false } ]
    question.save!

    @game.reload
    assert_equal "What does CSS stand for?", @game.game_questions.last.text
    assert_equal "Cascading Style Sheets", @game.game_questions.last.options.first.text
  end

  test "a game gets a short code that is unique" do
    assert_match(/\A[A-Z2-9]{5}\z/, @game.code)
    other = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)
    assert_not_equal @game.code, other.code
  end

  test "a new game is in the lobby" do
    assert @game.lobby?
    assert_equal 0, @game.position
    assert_nil @game.current_question
  end

  test "start opens the first question" do
    assert @game.start!
    @game.reload
    assert @game.open?
    assert_equal 1, @game.position
    assert_equal "Which HTTP status code means \"Too Many Requests\"?", @game.current_question.text
    assert_not_nil @game.game_questions.first.opened_at
  end

  test "a game with no active questions cannot start" do
    empty = Game.create_from_quiz!(Quiz.create!(title: "Empty"))
    assert_not empty.start!
    assert empty.lobby?
  end

  test "finish closes the question, and only an open question can be finished" do
    @game.start!
    assert @game.finish!
    @game.reload
    assert @game.closed?
    assert_not_nil @game.game_questions.first.closed_at
    assert_not @game.finish!, "a second Finish does nothing"
  end

  test "next opens the following question, and only after a closed one" do
    assert_not @game.next_question!, "the lobby has no next question"
    @game.start!
    assert_not @game.next_question!, "an open question is not closed yet"
    @game.finish!
    assert @game.next_question!
    @game.reload
    assert_equal 2, @game.position
    assert @game.open?
    assert_equal "Which protocol keeps a two-way connection?", @game.current_question.text
  end

I now understand the codebase. My plan:

- **Settings**: two integer columns on `quizzes` (`timer_minutes`, `timer_seconds`, default 0), validated and shown on the existing quiz form. The game copies the total seconds when it is created, the same way it copies questions.
- **Deadline**: `game_questions.opened_at` plus the limit. It is absolute and stored in the database, so reloads don't restart it and a server restart doesn't lose it.
- **Auto-finish**: the server closes an open question whose deadline has passed. This runs on every read of a game (big screen, live fragment, phone state, answers, buttons), so it doesn't depend on a worker. The big screen also asks for a refresh at 0:00, so the screen follows immediately. Answers after the deadline are refused.
- **Export**: unchanged, so the timer stays out of the JSON.

I'll start with the migration.

class Quiz < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :quiz
  has_many :games, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :quiz

  normalizes :title, with: ->(title) { title.strip }

  validates :title, presence: true, length: { maximum: 200 }
  # A cap keeps the number inside the column and the screen sensible.
  MAX_WINNERS_COUNT = 1000
  validates :winners_count, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than_or_equal_to: 1, less_than_or_equal_to: MAX_WINNERS_COUNT }

  # The time per question, as the moderator types it. 0 minutes and 0 seconds means
  # no timer. Seconds are 0 to 59, so the pair reads like a clock (1:30, 0:05).
  MAX_TIMER_MINUTES = 99
  MAX_TIMER_SECONDS = 59
  validates :timer_minutes, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0, less_than_or_equal_to: MAX_TIMER_MINUTES }
  validates :timer_seconds, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0, less_than_or_equal_to: MAX_TIMER_SECONDS }

  # The time per question in seconds: what a game copies when it starts.
  def time_limit_seconds
    timer_minutes.to_i * 60 + timer_seconds.to_i
  end
end
EOF

cd /app && python3 - <<'PYEOF'
import re, pathlib
p = pathlib.Path("app/models/game.rb")
s = p.read_text()

def rep(old, new, count=1):
    global s
    assert s.count(old) == count, (s.count(old), old[:80])
    s = s.replace(old, new)

# 1. header comment
rep("""# Ending ranks the players and stores each one's result (points, speed, place) on
# the player (see Leaderboard).""",
"""# With a time limit (see Quiz#time_limit_seconds), an open question closes by itself
# when its time is up, as if the moderator had clicked Finish. The deadline is the
# question's opened_at plus the limit, so it lives in the database: a reload does not
# restart it. Every read of the game first closes a question whose time is up (see
# #finish_if_time_up!), and an answer after the deadline is refused.
#
# Ending ranks the players and stores each one's result (points, speed, place) on
# the player (see Leaderboard).""")

# 2. validation
rep("""  validates :position, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0 }

  before_validation :assign_code, on: :create""",
"""  validates :position, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0 }
  validates :time_limit_seconds, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0 }

  before_validation :assign_code, on: :create""")

# 3. create_from_quiz copies the time limit
rep("""      game = create!(quiz: quiz, title: quiz.title)""",

  # clicked Finish (the question is closed at its deadline). Every read of the game
  # calls this first, so the screens and phones see the question closed without a
  # moderator. Returns true when it closed a question. Idempotent.
  def finish_if_time_up!
    return false unless timed?

    closed = transaction do
      reload
      close_when_time_up!
    end
    broadcast_change(moved: true) if closed
    closed
  end

  # Player actions.

  # Adds a player. Returns the player. It is unsaved, with errors, when the name
  # is not valid or the quiz is over.
  def join(name)
    player = players.new(name: name)
    saved = transaction do
      next false if Game.where(id: id, phase: "ended").exists?

      player.save && bump_revision!
    end
    broadcast_change if saved
    player
  end

  # Records the player's pick for the question on screen. The last pick counts,
  # and its time is kept (picked_at) for the speed ranking. Returns false when the
  # question is not open, or the option is not on it.
  def answer!(player, option)
    finish_if_time_up!
    saved = transaction do
      reload
      question = current_question
      now = Time.current
      next false unless open? && question && option.game_question_id == question.id && player.game_id == id
      next false if time_up?(now)

            .update!(game_option: option, picked_at: now)
      bump_revision!
    end
    broadcast_change if saved
    saved
  end

    self.code = self.class.unused_code if code.blank?
  end

    timed_out = false

require "test_helper"

# The time per question: the copy into a game, the countdown, the question closing
# by itself, and answers refused after the deadline. Time is travelled, so every
# number is exact.
class GameTimerTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  include ActionCable::TestHelper
  include GameFixtures

  BASE = Time.zone.local(2026, 11, 25, 10, 0, 0)

  setup do
    @quiz = build_quiz_with_questions # three active questions
    @quiz.update!(timer_minutes: 1, timer_seconds: 30)
    travel_to BASE - 600 do
      @game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)
    end
    @ann = nil
  end

  def start_at(time)
    travel_to(time) { @game.start! }
    @game.reload
  end

  def current_option(text)
    @game.current_question.options.find_by!(text: text)
  end

  test "a game copies the quiz's time per question when it is created" do
    assert_equal 90, @game.time_limit_seconds
    assert @game.timed?
  end

  test "changing the timer of the quiz later does not change a game" do
    @quiz.update!(timer_minutes: 0, timer_seconds: 5)
    assert_equal 90, @game.reload.time_limit_seconds
  end

  test "without a timer a question never closes by itself" do
    quiz = build_quiz_with_questions
    game = Game.create_from_quiz!(quiz)
    travel_to(BASE) { game.start! }
    travel_to(BASE + 86_400) do
      assert_not game.reload.timed?
      assert_nil game.deadline
      assert_nil game.seconds_left
      assert_not game.finish_if_time_up!
    end
    assert game.reload.open?
  end

  test "the deadline is the moment the question opened plus the time per question" do
    start_at(BASE)
    assert_equal BASE + 90, @game.deadline
    assert_equal 90, @game.seconds_left(BASE)
  end

  test "the seconds left round up, like a clock: 1:30 at the start, 0:00 at the end" do
    start_at(BASE)
    assert_equal 90, @game.seconds_left(BASE + 0.5)
    assert_equal 89, @game.seconds_left(BASE + 1)
    assert_equal 1, @game.seconds_left(BASE + 89.2)
    assert_equal 0, @game.seconds_left(BASE + 90)
    assert_equal 0, @game.seconds_left(BASE + 95)
  end

  test "there is no deadline outside an open question" do
    assert_nil @game.deadline, "the lobby has no question"
    start_at(BASE)
    travel_to(BASE + 5) { @game.finish! }
    assert_nil @game.reload.deadline, "a closed question has no countdown"
  end

  test "the question closes by itself at its deadline, as if Finish was clicked" do
    start_at(BASE)
    before = @game.progress

    travel_to(BASE + 89.999) do
      assert_not @game.finish_if_time_up!
    end
    assert @game.reload.open?

    travel_to(BASE + 90) do
      assert @game.finish_if_time_up!
    end
    @game.reload
    assert @game.closed?
    assert_equal 1, @game.position
    assert_equal before + 1, @game.progress
    assert_in_delta (BASE + 90).to_f, @game.game_questions.first.closed_at.to_f, 0.001
  end

  test "closing at the deadline happens once" do
    start_at(BASE)
    travel_to(BASE + 90) do
      assert @game.finish_if_time_up!
      assert_not @game.finish_if_time_up!
      assert_not @game.finish!, "the question is already closed"
    end
    assert @game.reload.closed?
  end

  test "the moderator can still finish earlier, and the timer then does nothing" do
    start_at(BASE)
    travel_to(BASE + 10) { assert @game.finish! }
    travel_to(BASE + 100) { assert_not @game.finish_if_time_up! }
    assert_in_delta (BASE + 10).to_f, @game.reload.game_questions.first.closed_at.to_f, 0.001
  end

  test "a time-up close tells the big screen and the phones" do
    start_at(BASE)
    travel_to(BASE + 90) do
      assert_broadcasts(@game.live_stream_name, 1) do
        assert_broadcasts(@game.play_stream_name, 1) { @game.finish_if_time_up! }
      end
    end
    travel_to(BASE + 91) do
      assert_no_broadcasts(@game.live_stream_name) { @game.finish_if_time_up! }
    end
  end

  test "a refused move still shows a question that the timer had closed" do
    start_at(BASE)
    travel_to(BASE + 90) do
      assert_broadcasts(@game.play_stream_name, 1) do
        assert_not @game.finish!, "the timer closed it first, so Finish has nothing to do"
      end
    end
    assert @game.reload.closed?
  end

  test "an answer before the deadline counts, and its time is kept" do
    start_at(BASE)
    ann = @game.join("Ann")
    travel_to(BASE + 89) { assert @game.answer!(ann, current_option("429")) }
    assert_equal BASE + 89, ann.answers.first.picked_at
    assert @game.reload.open?
  end

  test "an answer after the deadline is refused, even before anyone finished the question" do
    start_at(BASE)
    ann = @game.join("Ann")
    travel_to(BASE + 89) { assert @game.answer!(ann, current_option("429")) }

    travel_to(BASE + 90) do
      assert_not @game.answer!(ann, current_option("418"))
    end
    assert @game.reload.closed?, "the answer after the deadline closed the question"
    assert_equal "429", ann.answer_for(@game.game_questions.first).game_option.text
  end

  test "an answer exactly at the deadline is refused" do
    start_at(BASE)
    ann = @game.join("Ann")
    travel_to(BASE + 90) { assert_not @game.answer!(ann, current_option("429")) }
    assert_nil ann.answer_for(@game.game_questions.first)
  end

  test "the next question gets its own full time from when it opens" do
    start_at(BASE)
    travel_to(BASE + 90) { assert @game.finish_if_time_up! }
    travel_to(BASE + 95) { assert @game.next_question! }
    @game.reload
    assert @game.open?
    assert_equal 2, @game.position
    assert_equal BASE + 95, @game.game_questions.second.opened_at
    assert_equal BASE + 185, @game.deadline
    assert_equal 90, @game.seconds_left(BASE + 95)
  end

  test "a question closed by the timer can be ended as a quiz" do
    start_at(BASE)
    travel_to(BASE + 90) { assert @game.end_quiz! }
    assert @game.reload.ended?
  end

  test "reading the game again does not restart the clock" do
    start_at(BASE)
    travel_to(BASE + 30) do
      again = Game.find(@game.id)
      assert_equal BASE + 90, again.deadline
      assert_equal 60, again.seconds_left
    end
  end
end
EOF

# The time per question: "Timer minutes" and "Timer seconds", 0 and 0 for no timer.
class QuizTimerTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "a quiz has no timer by default: 0 minutes and 0 seconds" do
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Talk")
    assert_equal [ 0, 0 ], [ quiz.timer_minutes, quiz.timer_seconds ]
    assert_equal 0, quiz.time_limit_seconds
  end

  test "the time per question in seconds is minutes times 60 plus seconds" do
    quiz = Quiz.new(title: "Talk", timer_minutes: 1, timer_seconds: 30)
    assert_equal 90, quiz.time_limit_seconds
    quiz.timer_minutes = 0
    quiz.timer_seconds = 5
    assert_equal 5, quiz.time_limit_seconds
  end

  test "minutes are whole numbers from 0 to 99, seconds from 0 to 59" do
    quiz = Quiz.new(title: "Talk")
    [ [ 0, 0 ], [ 99, 59 ], [ 1, 30 ] ].each do |minutes, seconds|
      quiz.timer_minutes = minutes
      quiz.timer_seconds = seconds
      assert quiz.valid?, "#{minutes}:#{seconds} should be allowed"
    end

    [ [ -1, 0 ], [ 100, 0 ], [ 1.5, 0 ], [ nil, 0 ] ].each do |minutes, seconds|
      quiz.timer_minutes = minutes
      quiz.timer_seconds = seconds
      assert_not quiz.valid?, "minutes #{minutes.inspect} should be refused"
      assert_predicate quiz.errors[:timer_minutes], :any?
    end

    [ [ 0, -1 ], [ 0, 60 ], [ 0, 2.5 ], [ 0, nil ] ].each do |minutes, seconds|
      quiz.timer_minutes = minutes
      quiz.timer_seconds = seconds
      assert_not quiz.valid?, "seconds #{seconds.inspect} should be refused"
      assert_predicate quiz.errors[:timer_seconds], :any?
    end
  end

  test "the errors name the fields the way the form labels them" do
    quiz = Quiz.new(title: "Talk", timer_seconds: 75)
    quiz.valid?
    assert_equal [ "Timer seconds must be less than or equal to 59" ], quiz.errors.full_messages
  end
end

    @auth = moderator_headers
    @quiz = build_quiz_with_questions
    @quiz.update!(timer_minutes: 1, timer_seconds: 30)
    travel_to(BASE - 600) { @game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz) }
  end

  def countdown_text
    css_select("[data-controller='countdown'] [data-countdown-target='time']").first&.text
  end

  def countdown_deadline
    css_select("[data-controller='countdown']").first&.[]("data-countdown-deadline-value")&.to_i
  end

  def big_screen
    get "/moderate/games/#{@game.id}", headers: @auth
  end

  def open_question_at(time)
    travel_to(time) { @game.start! }
  end

  # --- settings ---

  test "the quiz form has the two timer fields, with 0 by default" do
    get "/moderate/quizzes/new", headers: @auth
    assert_select "label[for=quiz_timer_minutes]", text: "Timer minutes"
    assert_select "label[for=quiz_timer_seconds]", text: "Timer seconds"
    assert_select "input#quiz_timer_minutes[type=number][min='0'][value='0']"
    assert_select "input#quiz_timer_seconds[type=number][min='0'][max='59'][value='0']"
  end

  test "the settings show the time per question that is saved" do
    get "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/edit", headers: @auth
    assert_select "input#quiz_timer_minutes[value='1']"
    assert_select "input#quiz_timer_seconds[value='30']"
  end

  test "the settings save the time per question" do
    patch "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}", params: { quiz: { title: @quiz.title, winners_count: "3", timer_minutes: "2", timer_seconds: "5" } }, headers: @auth
    assert_redirected_to "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}"
    assert_equal [ 2, 5 ], [ @quiz.reload.timer_minutes, @quiz.timer_seconds ]
  end

  test "a new quiz can be given a timer, and 0 and 0 means none" do
    post "/moderate/quizzes", params: { quiz: { title: "Talk", winners_count: "3", timer_minutes: "0", timer_seconds: "45" } }, headers: @auth
    assert_equal 45, Quiz.find_by!(title: "Talk").time_limit_seconds
  end

  test "the settings refuse seconds above 59, with a message, and save nothing" do
    patch "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}", params: { quiz: { title: @quiz.title, winners_count: "3", timer_minutes: "1", timer_seconds: "75" } }, headers: @auth
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
    assert_select "[role=alert] li", text: "Timer seconds must be less than or equal to 59"
    assert_equal [ 1, 30 ], [ @quiz.reload.timer_minutes, @quiz.timer_seconds ]
  end

  test "the quiz page says how long each question has, or that there is no timer" do
    get "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}", headers: @auth
    assert_select ".meta", text: /1:30 per question/

    @quiz.update!(timer_minutes: 0, timer_seconds: 0)
    get "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}", headers: @auth
    assert_select ".meta", text: /No timer/
  end

  test "Start a game copies the time per question into the game" do
    post "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}/games", headers: @auth
    assert_equal 90, Game.order(:id).last.time_limit_seconds
  end

  # --- the big screen ---

  test "the big screen counts the open question down in M:SS, from the time per question" do
    open_question_at(BASE)
    travel_to(BASE) do
      big_screen
      assert_response :success
      assert_equal "1:30", countdown_text
      assert_equal(((BASE + 90).to_f * 1000).round, countdown_deadline)
      assert_select "[data-controller='countdown'][role='timer'][aria-label='Time left']"
    end
  end

  test "the countdown shows the time left, and 0:05 at five seconds" do
    open_question_at(BASE)
    travel_to(BASE + 10) do
      big_screen
      assert_equal "1:20", countdown_text
    end
    travel_to(BASE + 85) do
      big_screen
      assert_equal "0:05", countdown_text
    end
  end

  test "a reload does not restart the countdown" do
    open_question_at(BASE)
    travel_to(BASE + 40) do
      big_screen
      first = [ countdown_text, countdown_deadline ]
      big_screen
      assert_equal first, [ countdown_text, countdown_deadline ]
      assert_equal "0:50", first.first
    end
  end

  test "a quiz without a timer shows no countdown" do
    @quiz.update!(timer_minutes: 0, timer_seconds: 0)
    game = travel_to(BASE - 600) { Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz) }
    travel_to(BASE) { game.start! }
    get "/moderate/games/#{game.id}", headers: @auth
    assert_select ".countdown", count: 0
    assert_select "button", text: "Finish"
  end

  test "there is no countdown in the lobby, when the question is closed, or after the end" do
    get "/moderate/games/#{@game.id}", headers: @auth
    assert_select ".countdown", count: 0

    open_question_at(BASE)
    travel_to(BASE + 5) { @game.finish! }
    big_screen
    assert_select ".countdown", count: 0

    travel_to(BASE + 6) { @game.next_question! }
    travel_to(BASE + 7) { @game.finish! }
    travel_to(BASE + 8) { @game.next_question! }
    travel_to(BASE + 9) { @game.finish! }
    travel_to(BASE + 10) { @game.end_quiz! }
    big_screen
    assert_select ".countdown", count: 0
    assert_select "h1.screen__ended"
  end

  test "Finish still works before the deadline, and then the countdown is gone" do
    open_question_at(BASE)
    travel_to(BASE + 10) { post "/moderate/games/#{@game.id}/finish", headers: @auth }
    assert_redirected_to "/moderate/games/#{@game.id}"
    assert_nil flash[:alert]

    travel_to(BASE + 100) do
      big_screen
      assert_select ".countdown", count: 0
      assert_select "button", text: "Next"
    end
    assert_in_delta (BASE + 10).to_f, @game.reload.game_questions.first.closed_at.to_f, 0.001
  end

  test "at 0:00 the big screen shows the question closed, without anyone clicking Finish" do
    open_question_at(BASE)
    travel_to(BASE + 90) do
      big_screen
      assert_response :success
      assert_select ".countdown", count: 0
      assert_select "button", text: "Finish", count: 0
      assert_select "button", text: "Next"
      assert_select ".stage-option.is-correct", text: /429/
    end
    assert @game.reload.closed?
    assert_in_delta (BASE + 90).to_f, @game.game_questions.first.closed_at.to_f, 0.001
  end

  test "the live fragment changes at 0:00, so a screen that polls sees it closed" do
    open_question_at(BASE)
    etag = nil
    travel_to(BASE + 5) do
      get "/moderate/games/#{@game.id}/live", headers: @auth
      assert_response :success
      etag = response.headers["ETag"]

      get "/moderate/games/#{@game.id}/live", headers: @auth.merge("HTTP_IF_NONE_MATCH" => etag)
      assert_response :not_modified
    end

    travel_to(BASE + 90) do
      get "/moderate/games/#{@game.id}/live", headers: @auth.merge("HTTP_IF_NONE_MATCH" => etag)
      assert_response :success, "the view changed at 0:00, so it is not 304"
      assert_select ".countdown", count: 0
      assert_select "button", text: "Next"
    end
  end

  test "finishing by the button after 0:00 says the game has already moved on" do
    open_question_at(BASE)
    travel_to(BASE + 90) do
      post "/moderate/games/#{@game.id}/finish", headers: @auth
    end
    assert_redirected_to "/moderate/games/#{@game.id}"
    assert_equal "The game has already moved on. Look at the screen.", flash[:alert]
    assert @game.reload.closed?
  end

  # --- the phones ---

  test "phones never show the countdown or a clock time" do
    ann = open_session
    ann.post "/play/#{@game.code}/join", params: { player: { name: "Ann" } }
    open_question_at(BASE)
    travel_to(BASE + 10) do
      ann.get "/play/#{@game.code}"
      assert_equal 200, ann.response.status
      ann.assert_select ".play-option", minimum: 1
      ann.assert_select ".countdown", count: 0
      ann.assert_select "[data-countdown-deadline-value]", count: 0
      assert_no_match(/\d:\d\d/, Nokogiri::HTML(ann.response.body).at_css(".play__body").text)

      ann.get "/play/#{@game.code}/state"
      assert_no_match(/countdown|\d:\d\d/, ann.response.body)
    end
  end

  test "a phone's answer after 0:00 is refused, and the earlier one still counts" do
    ann = open_session
    ann.post "/play/#{@game.code}/join", params: { player: { name: "Ann" } }
    open_question_at(BASE)
    right = @game.current_question.options.find_by!(text: "429")
    wrong = @game.current_question.options.find_by!(text: "418")
    ann_player = @game.players.find_by!(name: "Ann")

    travel_to(BASE + 89) { ann.post "/play/#{@game.code}/answer", params: { game_option_id: right.id } }
    assert_equal "429", ann_player.answer_for(@game.game_questions.first).game_option.text

    travel_to(BASE + 90) do
      ann.post "/play/#{@game.code}/answer", params: { game_option_id: wrong.id }
      assert_redirected_to "/play/#{@game.code}"
      assert_equal "This question is closed.", ann.flash[:alert]
    end
    assert_equal "429", ann_player.answer_for(@game.game_questions.first).game_option.text
    assert @game.reload.closed?
  end

  test "after 0:00 the phone shows the result of the question" do
    ann = open_session
    ann.post "/play/#{@game.code}/join", params: { player: { name: "Ann" } }
    open_question_at(BASE)
    right = @game.current_question.options.find_by!(text: "429")
    travel_to(BASE + 89) { ann.post "/play/#{@game.code}/answer", params: { game_option_id: right.id } }

    travel_to(BASE + 91) do
      ann.get "/play/#{@game.code}"
      ann.assert_select "[role=status]", text: "Correct!"
      ann.assert_select ".play-option.is-correct", text: /429/
    end
  end
end
EOF
