cd /app && cat > docs/timer.md <<'EOF'
# Timer: time per question

Talks have tight schedules, so a quiz can give each question a time limit. The
moderator sets it in the quiz's **Settings**; the big screen counts the open question
down; when the time is up the question closes by itself, as if **Finish** had been
clicked. Players never see the timer. Nothing here calls an outside service.

## The setting

- Quiz form (\"New quiz\" and \"Settings\", the same form): a **Time per question**
  group with **Timer minutes** and **Timer seconds** (number fields, 0 by default).
  **0 minutes and 0 seconds means no timer.**
- Stored as two integers on `quizzes` (`timer_minutes`, `timer_seconds`).
  Minutes 0 to 99, seconds 0 to 59 (so the pair reads like a clock). Other values
  are refused with the field's message: "Timer seconds must be less than or equal
  to 59". A blank field is "Timer minutes is not a number".
- The quiz page shows it on the status line: "0:06 per question", or "No timer".
- **Not in the JSON export** (`quiz-json-format.md`). An imported quiz has no timer.

## What a game does with it

- **A game copies the total** (`games.time_limit_seconds`, minutes × 60 + seconds)
  when it is created, like its questions. Changing the quiz later changes neither a
  running game nor a played one. To use a new time, start a new game.
- The limit applies to **each question separately**: every question gets the full
  time from the moment it opens (**Start** or **Next**).

## The countdown

- **Deadline** = the question's `opened_at` + the limit. It is stored in the database,
  so a reload, a re-render or a server restart does not restart the clock. Nothing
  is computed from the time the page was loaded.
- The big screen shows the seconds left as **M:SS**, rounded up the way a clock
  shows it: 1:30 right after the start, 0:05 at five seconds, 0:00 at the end. It
  is shown only while a question is open, in the stage header next to
  "Question 1 of 3". The element is `div.countdown[role=timer][aria-label="Time left"]`
  with the time in its own `span`. The server draws the first value; the
  `countdown` Stimulus controller then counts down locally, from the absolute
  deadline (epoch milliseconds), every 200 ms.
- **Phones never get the countdown**: no element, no deadline, no clock time in the
  phone's HTML or its state fragment (tests check this).

## Closing at 0:00

The question closes in `Game#finish_if_time_up!` (the same move as Finish, with
`closed_at` set to the deadline, progress and revision bumped, both streams ticked).
It is checked **on every read of the game** instead of by a background job:

- every request for a game (the big screen page and its live fragment, the phone
  page and its state, the join and answer routes, every moderator button) first
  closes a question whose time is up (`set_game` in both controllers);
- a move (Finish, Next, End quiz) closes a timed-out question inside its own
  transaction first;
- an answer after the deadline is refused (`Game#answer!`, at or after the deadline),
  so a phone that taps late gets "This question is closed." and its earlier pick stands;
- when its countdown reaches 0:00, the big screen asks its live region for the view
  again (at most once a second, five times). The server then closes the question and
  the screen follows at once. The regular poll (about every 4 seconds) is the fallback.

Why not a worker: SQLite is the only store, and `bin/serve` runs one process. The
deadline is in the database, so the result is the same whenever somebody looks: the
answers counted are those before the deadline, and `closed_at` is the deadline itself.
The only thing that waits for a reader is the push to the screens, and every open
screen and phone polls anyway.

Edge cases (tested):

- **Finish before the time is up** works as before, and the timer then does nothing.
- **Finish after the time is up** (the button was still there a moment too late)
  says "The game has already moved on. Look at the screen." The question is closed.
- **Next** after the timer opens the next question with its own full time.
- **End quiz** after the timer works as usual.
- A question closed by the timer is no different from one closed by hand: same
  results, same speed ranking (answers only count before the deadline).

## Labels the QA tests rely on

- Settings: "Timer minutes", "Timer seconds" (labels, number fields with `min`/`max`),
  the group legend "Time per question".
- Quiz page: "0:06 per question" / "No timer" (status line).
- Big screen: the countdown text `M:SS`, e.g. "1:30" or "0:05"; no countdown text in
  the lobby, when closed, or after the end.
- Errors: "Timer seconds must be less than or equal to 59", "Timer minutes is not a number".

## Where the code lives

- `db/migrate/20261125030000_add_timer.rb`: the three columns.
- `app/models/quiz.rb`: the two fields' rules, `time_limit_seconds`.
- `app/models/game.rb`: `timed?`, `deadline`, `seconds_left`, `time_up?`,
  `finish_if_time_up!`, `close_when_time_up!` (in `move` too), the answer rule.
- `app/controllers/moderate/games_controller.rb`, `app/controllers/play_controller.rb`:
  `set_game` closes a timed-out question first.
- `app/helpers/games_helper.rb`: `countdown_text` (M:SS) and `countdown_tag`.
- `app/views/moderate/games/_screen.html.erb` (the countdown in the open phase),
  `app/views/moderate/quizzes/_form.html.erb` (the fields), `show.html.erb` (status line).
- `app/javascript/controllers/countdown_controller.js`: the local count-down and the
  0:00 ask.
- Styles: `.countdown`, `.stage-question__head` in `game.css` (big screen only);
  `.timer-field` in `moderator.css` (the moderator layout does not load `game.css`).

## Tests

- `test/models/game_timer_test.rb`: the copy, the rounding, the deadline, closing at
  the deadline and not before, Finish earlier, answers before and at/after the
  deadline, broadcasts, the next question's own time, a reload.
- `test/models/quiz_test.rb` (`QuizTimerTest`): defaults, bounds, messages.
- `test/models/quiz_export_test.rb` (`QuizExportTimerTest`): the export leaves the timer out.
- `test/integration/timer_test.rb`: the form and its errors, the big screen at each
  phase, a reload, 0:00 on the live fragment (ETag changes), phones (no clock, late
  answers refused, the result after 0:00).
- `test/system/timer_test.rb`: a real browser: the countdown counts down, the question
  closes at 0:00 with nobody clicking, phones show "Correct!" / "No answer" and no clock;
  a reload keeps the time.
- Checked by hand against `bin/serve` (production): a 6-second timer closed by itself,
  with a phone's correct answer shown.

## Insights

- The timer is a *setting copied into the game*, not read live (unlike the winners
  count, which applies until the winners are picked). The reason: a running game is
  a play, and a change in the settings mid-talk should not move the clock.
- Absolute deadlines beat countdowns that start from "now" on the client: a re-render
  of the live region (every 4 seconds when something changed) must not reset them.
- The server, not the browser, decides when a question is over. The browser only
  asks for a refresh at 0:00.
- Layouts load different stylesheets: the moderator's pages use `quizzy` and
  `moderator`; `game` is only in the big-screen and phone layouts. Put a style for a
  moderator form in `moderator.css`, or it silently does nothing there.
EOF

The docs are consistent. Before finishing, I want to revisit one design decision, because it affects the moderator's real workflow.

Right now a game copies the time per question when it is created. That means a moderator who starts a lobby and then realises they need a timer would have to start a new game, and every phone would have to join again. The Settings page reads as a live setting, and the winners count is read live for the same reason. The better rule is to read the time per question from the quiz when each question opens, and store that limit on the open question. Then changing the setting affects the next question, never the one already on screen. I'll make that change. The migration hasn't been committed or deployed, so I'll roll it back and move the column from `games` to `game_questions`.

  end

cd /app && cat > docs/timer.md <<'EOF'
# Timer: time per question

Talks have tight schedules, so a quiz can give each question a time limit. The
moderator sets it in the quiz's **Settings**; the big screen counts the open question
down; when the time is up the question closes by itself, as if **Finish** had been
clicked. Players never see the timer. Nothing here calls an outside service.

## The setting

- Quiz form ("New quiz" and "Settings", the same form): a **Time per question** group
  with **Timer minutes** and **Timer seconds** (number fields, 0 by default).
  **0 minutes and 0 seconds means no timer.**
- Stored as two integers on `quizzes` (`timer_minutes`, `timer_seconds`).
  Minutes 0 to 99, seconds 0 to 59 (so the pair reads like a clock). Other values are
  refused with the field's message, for example "Timer seconds must be less than or
  equal to 59"; a blank field gives "Timer minutes is not a number".
- The quiz page shows it on the status line: "0:06 per question", or "No timer".
- **Not in the JSON export** (`quiz-json-format.md`). An imported quiz has no timer.

## When the time is read

- **Each question reads the quiz's time when it opens** (**Start** or **Next**), and
  stores it with the question (`game_questions.time_limit_seconds`, total seconds).
  So:
  - a time set in the quiz after the game was created applies, as long as the
    question has not opened yet (for example, in the lobby, when the players are
    already joined);
  - a change while a question is open does not touch that question's clock; it applies
    to the next question to open;
  - a question that has no time (0) never closes by itself.
- The rule is the same as the winners count ("Number of winners"): read from the quiz
  at the moment it matters. The difference is that a question keeps what it was given.

## The countdown

- **Deadline** = the question's `opened_at` + its time limit (`GameQuestion#deadline`).
  It is in the database, so a reload, a re-render or a server restart does not restart
  the clock. Nothing is computed from the time a page was loaded.
- The big screen shows the seconds left as **M:SS**, rounded up the way a clock shows
  it: 1:30 right after the start, 0:05 at five seconds, 0:00 at the end. It is shown
  only while a question is open, in the stage header next to "Question 1 of 3". The
  element is `div.countdown[role=timer][aria-label="Time left"]` with the time in its
  own `span`. The server draws the first value; the `countdown` Stimulus controller then
  counts down locally from the absolute deadline (epoch milliseconds), every 200 ms.
- **Phones never get the countdown**: no element, no deadline and no clock time in the
  phone's HTML or its state fragment (tests check this).

## Closing at 0:00

The question closes in `Game#finish_if_time_up!`: the same move as Finish, with
`closed_at` set to the deadline, progress and revision bumped, and both streams ticked.
It is checked **on every read of the game** instead of by a background job:

- every request for a game (the big screen page and its live fragment, the phone page
  and its state, the join and answer routes, every moderator button) first closes a
  question whose time is up (`set_game` in both controllers). The check reads the game
  and writes only when the time is up, so an ordinary poll takes no write lock;
- a move (Finish, Next, End quiz) closes a timed-out question inside its own
  transaction first;
- an answer at or after the deadline is refused (`Game#answer!`), so a phone that taps
  late gets "This question is closed." and its earlier pick stands;
- when its countdown reaches 0:00, the big screen asks its live region for the view
  again (at most once a second, five times). The server then closes the question and the
  screen follows at once. The regular poll (about every 4 seconds) is the fallback.

Why no worker: SQLite is the only store, and `bin/serve` runs one process. The deadline
is in the database, so the result is the same whenever somebody looks: the answers
counted are those before the deadline, and `closed_at` is the deadline itself. The only
thing that waits for a reader is the push to the screens, and every open screen and
phone polls anyway.

Edge cases (tested):

- **Finish before the time is up** works as before, and the timer then does nothing.
- **Finish after the time is up** (the button was still there a moment too late) says
  "The game has already moved on. Look at the screen." The question is closed.
- **Next** after the timer opens the next question with its own time.
- **End quiz** after the timer works as usual.
- A question closed by the timer is no different from one closed by hand: same results,
  same speed ranking (only answers before the deadline count).

## Labels the QA tests rely on

- Settings: "Timer minutes", "Timer seconds" (labels; number fields with `min`/`max`),
  the group legend "Time per question".
- Quiz page: "0:06 per question" / "No timer" (status line).
- Big screen: the countdown text `M:SS`, e.g. "1:30" or "0:05"; no countdown text in the
  lobby, when closed, or after the end.
- Errors: "Timer seconds must be less than or equal to 59", "Timer minutes is not a number".

## Where the code lives

- `db/migrate/20261125030000_add_timer.rb`: `quizzes.timer_minutes`, `timer_seconds`,
  `game_questions.time_limit_seconds`.
- `app/models/quiz.rb`: the two fields' rules, `time_limit_seconds` (total seconds).
- `app/models/game_question.rb`: the limit's rule and `deadline`.
- `app/models/game.rb`: `deadline` (of the question on screen), `seconds_left`, `time_up?`,
  `finish_if_time_up!`, `close_when_time_up!` (also inside `move`), `quiz_time_limit_seconds`
  (read when a question opens), the answer rule.
- `app/controllers/moderate/games_controller.rb`, `app/controllers/play_controller.rb`:
  `set_game` closes a timed-out question first.
- `app/helpers/games_helper.rb`: `countdown_text` (M:SS) and `countdown_tag`.
- `app/views/moderate/games/_screen.html.erb` (the countdown in the open phase),
  `app/views/moderate/quizzes/_form.html.erb` (the fields), `show.html.erb` (status line).
- `app/javascript/controllers/countdown_controller.js`: the local count-down and the 0:00 ask.
- Styles: `.countdown`, `.stage-question__head` in `game.css` (big screen only);
  `.timer-field` in `moderator.css` (the moderator layout does not load `game.css`).

## Tests

- `test/models/game_timer_test.rb`: the time read at opening, a change while open and in
  the lobby, the rounding, the deadline, closing at the deadline and not before, Finish
  earlier, answers before and at/after the deadline, broadcasts, the next question's
  own time, a reload.
- `test/models/quiz_test.rb` (`QuizTimerTest`): defaults, bounds, messages.
- `test/models/quiz_export_test.rb` (`QuizExportTimerTest`): the export leaves the timer out.
- `test/integration/timer_test.rb`: the form and its errors, the big screen at each phase,
  a reload, 0:00 on the live fragment (the ETag changes), phones (no clock, late answers
  refused, the result after 0:00), a time set in the lobby.
- `test/system/timer_test.rb`: a real browser: the countdown counts down, the question
  closes at 0:00 with nobody clicking, phones show "Correct!" / "No answer" and no clock;
  a reload keeps the time.
- Checked by hand against `bin/serve` (production, two Chromium sessions): a 6-second timer
  counted down (0:06, then 0:05 after 1.6 s), the question closed by itself, and the
  phone showed "Correct!" with no clock.

## Insights

- Read the setting when it matters, and store what was decided. A question keeps the time
  it opened with, so the screen never jumps; the next question takes the new setting.
- Absolute deadlines beat countdowns that start from "now" on the client: a re-render of
  the live region must not reset them.
- The server, not the browser, decides when a question is over. The browser only asks for
  a refresh at 0:00.
- Layouts load different stylesheets: the moderator's pages use `quizzy` and `moderator`;
  `game` is only in the big-screen and phone layouts. Put a style for a moderator form in
  `moderator.css`, or it silently does nothing there.
EOF

messages.content:
The timer is implemented and verified: unit, integration and browser tests pass, and it works end to end under `bin/serve` in production mode. I'm submitting now.

Summary of the work:

**What was already there:** `/app` was not empty. It held an earlier, uncommitted Quizzy (moderator quizzes, the live game, prizes, import/export). I built the timer on top of it and discarded nothing.

**Timer behaviour**
- **Settings:** "Timer minutes" and "Timer seconds" (number fields, default 0) on the same form as "Number of winners", so they appear on both "New quiz" and "Settings". 0 and 0 means no timer. Minutes accept 0–99 and seconds 0–59; anything else gets a field error.
- **Big screen:** shows the countdown as M:SS (for example 1:30, 0:05) while a question is open. The browser counts it down locally from an absolute deadline, so a reload or re-render doesn't restart it.
- **Phones:** no countdown, no deadline, no clock text anywhere in the phone page or its state fragment.
- **Auto-finish at 0:00:** the question closes as if Finish was clicked, and "Finish" still works earlier. The server closes a timed-out question on every read of the game, and answers at or after the deadline are refused. The big screen also asks for a refresh when it hits 0:00.
- **Export:** the timer is left out of the JSON; an import gets no timer.

**Decisions you may want to review**
- **Time is read when each question opens, not when the game is created.** A moderator can set the timer in the lobby, after the phones have joined, and it applies to the first question. A question on screen keeps its own limit, so a settings change never moves its clock.
- **Seconds are validated (0–59), not normalised.** Entering 90 seconds gives an error instead of silently becoming 1:30.
- **No background worker.** Closing happens on the next read, using the stored deadline, so the result is the same regardless of who looks. The big screen triggers it at 0:00, and phones and screens also poll every few seconds.
- **Finish after the timer has already closed the question** shows "The game has already moved on. Look at the screen."

**Verification**
- Unit and integration tests: 234 pass (43 new). System tests in Chromium: 33 pass (2 new, including a countdown that visibly counts down and a question that closes with nobody clicking).
- RuboCop and Brakeman are clean. No gems were added, and `bundle check` passes offline.
- Against a fresh `bin/serve` in production mode, a two-session Chromium run showed a 6-second timer at 0:06, then 0:05 after 1.6 s, closed by itself, with the phone showing "Correct!" and no clock.
- I also checked the settings layout at desktop and phone widths. This caught a real bug: the moderator's pages don't load `game.css`, so the form styles moved to `moderator.css`.

**Housekeeping**
- I removed the production databases and `public/assets` left by my test runs, so the next `bin/serve` starts clean. A stale production database would have been missing the new column.
- Docs: a new `docs/timer.md`, plus updates to `live-game.md`, `quiz-json-format.md`, `design-notes.md` and `README.md`.
- Changes are left uncommitted in the working tree, like the earlier work.
